cells.tense: The change is already moving, and this is where you watch it take shape.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Set down on paper what you're building — the part that moves soon and the part that waits — then follow that page instead of your mood, and leave the unforceable alone.
cells.core:
You can feel which piece of a thing counts before you can explain it, and you build in the world at the speed that sense allows — slow, and it doesn't quit. The structure goes in underneath the change instead of being jammed on top of it. Method here doesn't fight the pace. It rides it.

Watch where you reach for another tool when the page in your hand would serve. That's mood talking, not method. Take the change you're actually building and put it down in writing — what moves now, what waits — then follow that page rather than the mood, and leave the part you can't force where it sits. Practice, not policy: tomorrow you can look again and choose differently.
cells.sheetLine: You see what counts and build at its pace.

cells.tense: A change that hasn't happened yet is already being forced, and it isn't ready to be built.
cells.act: teach what you feel by doing it with others
cells.ask: Do the first small step of the change alongside one other person instead of pitching the finished version. Let their question bend what you're making.
cells.core:
The pushing has outrun the perceiving. A change that hasn't arrived is already being forced into place, and the harder you push, the less room the quiet sense gets — the plan has become the answer. Building this fast stops being building. It turns into bracing against the thing you're waiting for, and nothing moves while you brace.

Hand the change to someone. Take one person and do the first small step alongside them rather than describing the finished version. Let their question bend what you're making — a rehearsal, not a launch. What you pass on is the part you can't yet put into words, and their asking makes it sayable. The pace matters more than the plan.

cells.tense: A decision about what to build already got made, and pushing on it has gone quiet.
cells.act: charge forward on the decision you made
cells.ask: Move on the decision about the change you already made — the next concrete step, no review first — because sitting with it longer is how it stalls, not how it clears.
cells.core:
This got tired. A decision about the change was made — you know which one — and since then the building has gone still, as if it were waiting on a better moment or a clearer sign. The sign already came. What's left in that place is waiting.

Don't try to feel your way back to it; the energy goes into the doer instead. Take that decision and move on it, concrete enough that you'd notice if it didn't happen. Not a plan, not a review. The first move is the whole of it. The point isn't the step; deciding and doing come back into the same person, because at the moment they're standing in different rooms.

cells.tense: The building keeps happening in your hands, and you'd tell it as someone else's.
cells.act: feed the drive a little at a time
cells.ask: Find where the work you're carrying is running you down, then give it back a portion of what it spends — a little at a time, not a push.
cells.core:
The building keeps happening — a hand on the structure, the steady pressure that turns a plan into a thing — and if someone asked who's doing it, you'd say it runs itself, or that someone else began it. The one who sees what counts is the same one carrying the load. That part of the story has been filed outside your own account of yourself.

The fire needs tending, not more proof. Find one change you're already carrying and notice, quietly, where it's running you down — then give it back a portion of what it spends, a little at a time, and let today hold only that. You learn what you've been holding by holding it on purpose. The work was yours the whole time; putting a hand on it is how you find out for certain.
cells.sheetLine: The work is yours and you tell it as borrowed.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the reader can tell when a change is load-bearing before they start — the record only shows that the knowing is there to be attended to, not what they already know. A reader could reasonably say the change they keep pushing is the one thing that must move, and waiting is how it stalls. The asks survive being wrong because they practice method and courage, not accuracy. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line that makes slow persistence sound like a fixed trait rather than a move they can put down.
